newsitem.title: LEBANON: Syria to finance projects in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Syria to finance projects in Lebanon.

text.p: Syria will build a sports complex in south Lebanon on the site of a former Israeli detention camp, Lebanese officials on Thursday quoted Syrian President Hafez al-Assad as saying.

Officials close to outgoing parliament speaker Nabih Berri, said Assad told him on Wednesday in Damascus that Syria would donate $10 million for the 10-hectare (25-acre) complex in the village of Ansar and other projects.
Israel held thousands of Lebanese and Arab prisoners at Ansar camp until 1985 when it pulled out the bulk of its forces from Lebanon and set up a 15-km (nine-mile) deep border occupation zone.

Other projects Syria would fund included a museum and a commemorative stone in the southern village of Qana where Israeli shelling killed 103 civilians taking refuge at a U.N. base in April, the officials said.

The Qana massacre took place during a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon against pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas. Qana is about eight km (five miles) north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, while Ansar is farther north.
Syria would also build a cultural centre in the southern port of Tyre, another in southeastern Lebanon and an orphanage in the coastal village of Sarafand, the officials said.
Syria, which has some 35,000 troops in Lebanon, is Beirut's main power broker.
